DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia

The clinical picture of a 7-month continuous course of auditory hallucinations (predating the depressive symptoms by 3 months) alongside negative symptoms (concentration issues, emptiness) and negative family history strongly supports a primary psychotic disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features, which requires concurrent mood symptoms during the psychotic episode. The lack of mania further rules out Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features.
